svg.title: The three verification loops Anthropic used to port its Messages API to Rust
svg.text: Three loops, one source of truth: the running Python service
How Anthropic organised agents and engineers, per its 25 November 2026 engineering post.

g.text: Inner loop · seconds to minutes · agent in a sandbox
Guess a cause, write a request or model reply that triggers it, run it through Python and Rust.
Input check runs in under a second. Edit Rust until both match, add a test, open a pull request.
Who decides: the local verifier, then a human reviewer on the pull request.
Outer loop · hours to days · shadowed production traffic
Each request runs on both versions; the model is called once and its reply replayed to Rust.
Differences are logged as fingerprints (step, prompt piece, first differing byte, lengths), never as text.
A script groups them every 10 to 30 minutes and hands each new kind to a worker agent.
Fingerprint still there after a fix ships? Back to the inner loop.
Memory loop · ongoing · engineers' corrections become rules
Rejected fixes turn into notes later agents read. Repeated review comments become CLAUDE.md rules.
Some lessons become hard checks: drift tests, lint bans, and a merge check that blocks Python
changes without a matching Rust change or an exemption.
Who decides: humans, on what counts as correct.

svg.text: Source: Anthropic, "Migrating our Messages API to Rust". Diagram: The Dispatch.
